name: Eggs
anchor: per-commodity sovereign metallic-contamination schedules for terrestrial animal foods — Hong Kong Cap. 132V Part 2 Schedule (the only credible instrument on the register with a complete meat, poultry and egg panel), EU Regulation (EU) 2023/915 for cadmium in muscle meat, and FSANZ Schedule 19 for lead in muscle meat; canned forms additionally carry the canned-foods tin maximum level, and the plant-protein analogue row reads across from EU and Hong Kong pulse, soy and cereal commodity maximum levels
native_basis_label: as sold, edible portion (wet weight), shell excluded; dried and powdered egg is assessed on the product as sold with no reconstitution conversion; because drying CONCENTRATES the egg solids roughly fourfold, applying the whole-egg maximum level to the powder as sold is the stricter treatment in this direction, and it is never reversed to recover head-room
scope_note: Poultry eggs for human consumption — hen, duck, quail and goose — as shell eggs, liquid whole egg, liquid yolk, liquid white, and dried or powdered egg. Traditionally preserved eggs (lime-preserved, century, salted duck egg) are IN scope and are the reason both Hong Kong lead entries are named: the historical alkaline curing mixes for century eggs used lead oxide as a processing aid, which is a live adulteration pathway and mandates lot testing of any preserved-egg lot. Egg-containing composite foods (mayonnaise, custard, baked goods) route to their own categories. Egg products marketed for ages 0-5 route to Category 1. Fish roe routes to Category 6.
basis_guard: (wet weight|portion ordinarily consumed|product as placed on market|food as listed|as sold|as consumed|commodity|edible part|fresh weight)
basis_guard_note: Category 11 is a dietary as-sold wet-weight category. The guard admits only register rows whose basis is a food-matrix content basis (wet weight, portion ordinarily consumed, product as placed on market, commodity, edible part, food as listed in the Cap 132V schedule). It rejects, by construction, food-contact specific-migration limits, toy and article element-migration limits, animal-feed 12%-moisture bases, dry-matter fertiliser limits, colour-additive ingredient purity specifications, and drinking-water statutory limits. A migration or purity-specification number is not a maximum level for a food and must never anchor a meat, poultry, or egg row.
method: HMTc Method v2.0 (government-limit-only initial setting: the strictest applicable sovereign maximum level for this exact product form in its native basis; disclosed read-across where the exact cell is unregulated; control where neither a sovereign number nor a supportable near-neighbour analogue exists; never occurrence-derived)

Pb.basis: as sold, edible portion excluding shell (wet weight)
Pb.label: Hong Kong Cap. 132V lead maximum level for poultry eggs and for lime-preserved eggs; both entries sit at 200 ug/kg
Pb.substantiation: Hong Kong Cap. 132V Part 2 Schedule is the only credible sovereign instrument on this register that sets a lead maximum level for eggs, and it does so twice: poultry eggs 0.2 mg/kg and lime-preserved eggs 0.2 mg/kg. Both are named so that the preserved-egg form is covered explicitly rather than by silence. The EU sets no egg lead maximum level and Codex CXS 193's egg rows are absent from this register; neither omission licenses borrowing the stricter 100 ug/kg muscle-meat value, because meat is not an applicable scope for an egg and Method v2.0 selects the strictest APPLICABLE sovereign value, not the strictest value in the instrument. That this ceiling sits above the muscle-meat ceiling is a fact about the sovereign instruments and is disclosed rather than harmonised away.

Cd.basis: as sold, edible portion excluding shell (wet weight)
Cd.label: read-across from the poultry-meat cadmium maximum level in the same sovereign instrument (Hong Kong Cap. 132V, 50 ug/kg)
Cd.substantiation: No credible sovereign government sets a cadmium maximum level for eggs: Hong Kong Cap. 132V regulates poultry eggs for lead and mercury but not cadmium, and the EU, Codex, FSANZ, UK, US and Health Canada set no egg cadmium value at all. The exact cell is therefore unregulated. The nearest applicable sovereign cell is the cadmium maximum level for meat of poultry in the SAME instrument and for the SAME producing animal (0.05 mg/kg), adopted by disclosed read-across. The looser poultry-liver (0.5 mg/kg) and poultry-kidney (1.0 mg/kg) cadmium values were considered and rejected: an egg is not offal, and cadmium's affinity for renal and hepatic tissue is exactly why those rows are looser. Choosing the stricter muscle-meat analogue is what the method requires.

tAs.basis: as sold, edible portion excluding shell (wet weight)
tAs.label: read-across from the poultry-meat total-arsenic maximum level in the same sovereign instrument (Hong Kong Cap. 132V, 500 ug/kg)
tAs.substantiation: No credible sovereign government sets a total-arsenic maximum level for eggs. Hong Kong Cap. 132V regulates meat of poultry at 0.5 mg/kg total arsenic, the nearest applicable sovereign cell for a product of the same producing animal, adopted by disclosed read-across. The organoarsenical feed-additive pathway that motivates the poultry inorganic-arsenic control applies equally to laying flocks, so the same reflex speciation obligation is carried into this row's iAs cell.

iAs.rationale: No credible sovereign government sets an inorganic-arsenic maximum level for eggs or egg products. Every credible inorganic-arsenic instrument on the register is scoped elsewhere: EU 2023/915 and EU 2025/1891 to rice, rice products, fruit juices, infant food and seafood; UK, Health Canada and US FDA to rice-based and juice matrices; Hong Kong Cap. 132V to rice and aquatic animals. A NOT-MATERIAL determination is deliberately REJECTED for this cell rather than adopted for convenience: organoarsenical feed additives (roxarsone, nitarsone, arsanilic acid, carbarsone) were lawfully administered to poultry and swine in major producing markets within living memory and are documented to leave arsenic residues in edible tissue, so the programme will not make the affirmative claim that no inorganic-arsenic pathway exists in terrestrial animal food. For the ruminant rows, where no equivalent additive history applies, the absence of that pathway does not by itself substantiate a not-material determination either, because neither a sovereign number nor a supportable near-neighbour analogue exists for the cell in any case. Because no sovereign number governs the cell and no near-neighbour cell is a supportable analogue (a rice or seafood inorganic-arsenic maximum level describes a different contamination mechanism entirely), the cell is a control: testing is mandatory and no ceiling is invented.
iAs.reference_method: Inorganic arsenic by anion-exchange HPLC-ICP-MS speciation. Speciation is reflex-triggered on every lot whose total-arsenic screen is quantifiable above the method limit of quantitation, and unconditionally on the first lot from any new supplier, slaughter establishment, or country of origin. Any quantifiable inorganic arsenic is escalated to the certification committee together with the feed-additive and origin declaration; the lot cannot be released on an inorganic-arsenic result while the escalation is open, and a total-arsenic result at or above the binding total-arsenic maximum level is a hard stop irrespective of speciation.

tHg.basis: as sold, edible portion excluding shell (wet weight)
tHg.label: Hong Kong Cap. 132V total-mercury maximum level for poultry eggs
tHg.substantiation: Hong Kong Cap. 132V Part 2, mercury expressed as total mercury, poultry eggs, 0.05 mg/kg = 50 ug/kg. This is a direct sovereign maximum level for the exact cell, not a read-across.

MeHg.rationale: Methylmercury is formed by microbial methylation in aquatic sediment and biomagnifies through aquatic food webs. The egg of a terrestrial bird carries no methylation pathway and no aquatic trophic transfer, and methylmercury is in any event a component of total mercury (MeHg <= tHg), so it is bounded by and controlled through the published total-mercury cell (50 ug/kg total mercury, Hong Kong Cap. 132V poultry eggs). No separate methylmercury ceiling is published because none would bind below the total-mercury ceiling and none is set by any credible sovereign government for this product form.
MeHg.reference_method: Not measured routinely. Bounded by the total-mercury cell; methylmercury speciation by HPLC-ICP-MS is reflex-triggered only where a lot's total-mercury result approaches the binding total-mercury maximum level, or where the formulation incorporates a fish, fish-meal, or marine-derived ingredient, which would additionally route the lot to the Category 6 seafood mercury ceilings.
MeHg.regulatory_basis: No credible sovereign government sets a methylmercury content limit for meat, poultry, game, eggs, or meat analogues. The credible methylmercury instruments (EU 2023/915 Annex I section 3.3, US FDA CPG 540.600, FSANZ Schedule 19, Hong Kong Cap. 132V) are scoped exclusively to fish, crustaceans, molluscs and other aquatic animals. Methylmercury is a species of, and arithmetically bounded by, total mercury.
MeHg.jurisdictions_checked: EU (Regulation (EU) 2023/915 Annex I); UK retained contaminants law; Codex CXS 193-1995; US FDA (CPG 540.600); FSANZ Australia New Zealand Food Standards Code Schedule 19; Health Canada; Hong Kong Cap. 132V Food Adulteration (Metallic Contamination) Regulations Part 2 Schedule — none sets a methylmercury limit for a terrestrial animal food, an egg, or a plant-protein meat analogue.

Ni.rationale: No credible sovereign government sets a nickel maximum level for eggs or egg products. The EU nickel maximum levels recorded on the register (the eu2024_ni_* family) are drawn exclusively over plant matrices — cereals, pulses, legume, leafy and root vegetables, tree nuts, oilseeds, cocoa — and the only other credible nickel values are drinking-water statutory limits and a food-contact specific-migration limit, both in bases that cannot govern the content of a food. A plant-commodity nickel maximum level is not a supportable near-neighbour for animal muscle tissue, which accumulates nickel by a different route and at a different order of magnitude, so no read-across is available and no ceiling is invented.
Ni.reference_method: Total nickel by ICP-MS on every certified lot, trended per SKU and per production line. Escalation is triggered by a result above the SKU's established rolling upper control limit, or by an increasing trend across three consecutive lots, and directs the investigation to nickel-bearing stainless contact surfaces (grinders, mincers, brine injectors, forming plates). No numeric ceiling is published because no sovereign instrument compels one.

Sn.rationale: Inorganic tin in food is a tinplate-packaging pathway: tin migrates into the food from the internal surface of an unlacquered or damaged tinplate can, which is why every credible sovereign tin maximum level on the register is written against canned food rather than against the food itself. Shell eggs, liquid egg and dried egg in carton, tub or bag packaging is not packed in tinplate, so the pathway that the canned-food maximum levels exist to control is absent and no sovereign number governs the cell. A lot of this product form that is retorted or packed in a metal can is not certified against this row at all: it is certified against the canned-meats row, whose tin cell carries the binding canned-foods maximum level. No tin ceiling is invented for the non-canned form.
Sn.reference_method: Total tin by ICP-MS on every certified lot. Any quantifiable tin in a lot declared as non-metal-packed triggers a packaging and contact-surface investigation (can or closure liner, tinned equipment, solder) before release, and re-routes the lot to the canned-meats row if metal packaging is found.

Al.rationale: No credible sovereign government sets an aluminium maximum level for meat, poultry, game or eggs. The credible aluminium values on the register are drinking- and bottled-water statutory limits (EU 2020/2184, US FDA 21 CFR 165.110, Health Canada), a food-contact specific-migration limit (EU 10/2011), toy element-migration limits, and the FSANZ Schedule 19 aluminium maximum levels for infant formula. None can anchor this row: the water and migration values are in a different basis, and an adult food must not borrow an infant-formula maximum level (products marketed for ages 0-5 route to Category 1 by the taxonomy boundary rule). No read-across is supportable and no ceiling is invented.
Al.reference_method: Total aluminium by ICP-MS on every certified lot, trended per SKU. Escalation is triggered by a result above the SKU's established rolling upper control limit or by an increasing trend across three consecutive lots, and directs the investigation to aluminium contact surfaces and packaging (foil, trays, aluminium cookware, aluminium-containing processing aids). No numeric ceiling is published because no sovereign instrument compels one.

Cr.screen_note: Total chromium in food is dominated by benign trivalent chromium, an essential trace element; the health-relevant species is hexavalent chromium, which does not persist in this matrix (see the Cr-VI cell). The Hong Kong Cap. 132V total-chromium maximum level is a real sovereign limit and is published here, but it is recorded as a SCREEN: it is a contact-surface and equipment-leaching tripwire, not a standalone protective ceiling, and it is excluded from the firm-limit count.
Cr.basis: as sold, edible portion excluding shell (wet weight)
Cr.label: read-across from the poultry-meat total-chromium maximum level in the same sovereign instrument (Hong Kong Cap. 132V, 1000 ug/kg), published as a screen
Cr.substantiation: No credible sovereign government sets a total-chromium maximum level for eggs. The nearest applicable sovereign cell is meat of poultry (Hong Kong Cap. 132V, 1 mg/kg), adopted by disclosed read-across and published as a screen for the reasons given in the Cr-VI cell.

Cr-VI.rationale: Hexavalent chromium is not stable in this matrix. Liquid, shell and dried egg is a wet, reducing, protein- and thiol-rich medium; Cr(VI) is reduced to Cr(III) by tissue reductants (cysteine, glutathione, ascorbate) and by the acid and heat of digestion and cooking, so a Cr(VI) figure reported on such a matrix is an artifact of the extraction chemistry of the total-chromium screen rather than a measurement of a species that persists in the food. The determination follows the same reference-method adjudication recorded for the hexavalent-chromium cell in the infant-formula category (data/workbench standards Cr-VI adjudication), applied here to an animal-tissue matrix. Hexavalent chromium is in any event a species of, and bounded by, the published total-chromium screen (Cr-VI <= total Cr).
Cr-VI.reference_method: Not measured routinely. Bounded by the total-chromium screen (Cr cell). Alkaline-extraction Cr(VI) determination (IC-ICP-MS) is reflex-triggered only where the total-chromium screen exceeds the published screen value, in which case the investigation is directed at stainless-steel contact surfaces, grinders, and brine or marinade equipment rather than at the raw material.
Cr-VI.regulatory_basis: No credible sovereign government sets a hexavalent-chromium content limit for any food. Every credible Cr(VI) instrument on the register is an article, textile, leather, toy-migration, tattoo-ink, fertiliser or electrical-equipment limit in a non-food basis, and applying one to a food matrix would be a basis conflation the compiler's basis guard rejects. Total chromium is regulated for meat and poultry by Hong Kong Cap. 132V and is published here as a screen.
Cr-VI.jurisdictions_checked: EU (Regulation (EU) 2023/915; Regulation (EU) 10/2011; Directive 2009/48/EC; REACH restrictions); UK; Codex CXS 193-1995; US FDA; FSANZ Schedule 19; Health Canada; Hong Kong Cap. 132V Part 2 Schedule — none sets a hexavalent-chromium content limit for food.
